title: A fair shuffle swaps each card with a random earlier one
body: Fisher-Yates picks each position from the end and swaps it with a uniformly chosen position at or before it, producing every permutation with exactly equal probability. Naive 'swap with any position' shuffles are provably biased, some orders appearing more often. The 1938 pencil-and-paper method, modernised by Knuth, is still the correct three lines.
source_hint: Fisher and Yates (1938); Knuth TAOCP vol. 2
